dialogue.content: How do I keep clay from drying out between weekly classes?
Wrap pieces in damp paper towels inside a sealed bag, and check moisture midweek.
A friend said a weekend glaze workshop signup is amazing and asked if the class is worth it. Should I grab that one tourist-style ticket? It is not my regular evening studio.
Treat a one-off weekend workshop signup as a fun ticket decision. It does not automatically say anything about your recurring evening schedule.
Friend said it is amazing, but I only care whether that single workshop class signup is worth it.
My weekday wheel sessions at the studio often run past eleven. I get home wired and it takes a while to settle.
Studio nights that run past eleven can push bedtime later even when the making itself is enjoyable.
Best way to clean tools without clogging the sink?
Wipe scraps into the trash first, then rinse in a bucket and dump settled water outside if allowed.
A few times a week I help shape loaves before sunrise at a friend's shop. I need solid sleep the night before or I am useless at the oven.
Pre-dawn oven shifts make the prior night non-negotiable. Staying up late beforehand will tax that.
How do I choose between hobbies when both feel meaningful?
Rank by recovery cost, not by which one sounds cooler to friends.
People keep saying an extra late evening class signup would be amazing and asking if it is worth it.
An extra late evening class signup only helps if it does not steal sleep you already allocated elsewhere. Amazing is not the test.
I compared two more options and kept the details.
That gives you another detail to weigh against your priorities.
The studio opened another late evening class signup on nights before my bakery mornings. Friend said it is amazing. Should I add it — is it worth it?
